memory_update.text: SPSC is the cleanest Layer 2B relationship in this chunk: retailer-supplier EDI/compliance transaction network with externally cited 120,000 trading partners and 95% recurring revenue; primary-source validation still required.

TGT should remain a reference demand signal, not an alpha candidate in this underfollowed chunk; its supply-chain issues help define nodes for inventory visibility, upstream buffers, supplier responsiveness, and sourcing diversification.

TRAK requires the highest-priority primary-source check among speculative-shadow candidates: supplier count, FSMA 204 timing, named retailer mandates, recurring revenue, retention, and customer concentration.
DSGX needs consumer-exposure disaggregation before ranking: retail/ecommerce/grocery revenue should be separated from freight-forwarding, customs, carrier, and general logistics software exposure.

THS private-label thesis depends on whether retailer private-label share gains are visible in TreeHouse volume, utilization, pricing, and margin rather than only in industry-level private-label commentary.

AGYS and PAR should be evaluated with a software-quality lens: recurring mix, ARR or subscription revenue, retention, implementation backlog, customer concentration, and hardware drag are gating variables.

CHEF, SXT, MGPI, SLGN, GFF, FBIN, and WMS are plausible second-order Consumer nodes but currently lack enough provided evidence for strong chokepoint claims; keep as hypotheses pending filings and segment validation.
For all candidates, add live market-cap, liquidity, short interest, analyst coverage, and institutional ownership checks before confirming underfollowed status.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk away from headline consumer brands and toward embedded operating infrastructure, supplier-compliance networks, private-label capacity, restaurant/hospitality workflow software, specialty distribution, formulation inputs, packaging, and repair/remodel channel suppliers. The strongest direct ticker relationship in the provided evidence is SPSC as retailer-supplier transaction infrastructure. TRAK, DSGX, THS, AGYS, PAR, CHEF, SXT, MGPI, SLGN, GFF, FBIN, and WMS remain research candidates with varying evidence quality; most require primary-source validation before graduating beyond hypothesis status. No buy/sell recommendation is made.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify current trading-partner count, recurring-revenue percentage, net retention, churn, retailer/customer concentration, supplier wallet share, tariff-related spending delays versus churn, and whether integrations remain costly to replace.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K, 10-Q, investor presentation, earnings call transcript, and customer metrics; compare recurring revenue, revenue growth, retention, active customers, and guidance commentary against the March 2026 external deep dive.
ticker_relationships.node: Retailer-supplier transaction network / EDI compliance layer
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPS Commerce maps directly to the retail EDI and supplier-compliance plumbing layer that connects retailers, brands, distributors, and suppliers through order, invoice, shipment, and compliance workflows. If retailer inventory discipline, tariff-driven supplier changes, omnichannel replenishment, and food/grocery compliance complexity rise, this node can become more operationally important.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify supplier-count growth, recurring revenue, revenue per supplier, customer concentration, FSMA 204 deadline sensitivity, retention, named retailer mandates, and whether onboarding converts into durable SaaS revenue.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Use primary filings and company releases to confirm customer concentration, SaaS/revenue-recognition profile, traceability-network scale, mandate language, and churn; search for retailer or distributor references that independently confirm supplier onboarding.
ticker_relationships.node: Grocery and food-retail traceability / supplier compliance data
ticker_relationships.relationship: ReposiTrak maps to supplier documentation, food-traceability, and retailer compliance data. The candidate relationship is strongest if grocery retailers or food distributors require suppliers to use a shared compliance network for FSMA 204-style traceability and documentation workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Measure revenue tied to retailers, consumer-goods suppliers, ecommerce, grocery, and omnichannel fulfillment versus freight-forwarding, customs-only, and non-consumer logistics use cases.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest annual report and investor deck; segment product modules by consumer-retail exposure, identify retailer/ecommerce customer examples, and compare organic growth versus acquisition-driven growth.
ticker_relationships.node: Cross-border retail logistics and trade-compliance messaging
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes maps to logistics network software, customs/trade-compliance messaging, carrier connectivity, and shipment-data workflows that sit adjacent to consumer retail, ecommerce, grocery, and omnichannel fulfillment. The consumer relationship is plausible but partly indirect because the company also serves broader logistics and trade customers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify customer concentration, category exposure, plant utilization, contract duration, pricing pass-through, margin sensitivity to commodities, and whether private-label share gains are translating into volume or margin improvement.

ticker_relationships.node: Private-label food manufacturing and retailer-controlled brand capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: TreeHouse Foods maps to retailer private-label food manufacturing capacity. The relationship is that grocers and mass retailers may rely on scaled private-label manufacturers as they push value-tier offerings, shelf control, and retailer-owned brands against national brands.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify recurring revenue mix, SaaS transition progress, hotel/casino customer concentration, implementation stickiness, net retention, sales-cycle sensitivity, and exposure to travel capex cycles.

The relationship is strongest where front-desk, booking, POS, payments, inventory, and guest-service workflows create switching costs after implementation.

Its inventory-visibility challenges, sourcing infrastructure, cautious inventory stance, and upstream receive/distribution center investments help define the nodes that supplier-connectivity, logistics, forecasting, and private-label candidates may serve.
